content:
B0–B2 accepted. All three of your calls are correct — keep them as built.

1. TEMPORAL MULTIPLIER — your reading stands. The doc's prose and the doc's own unit test contradict each other; the test is the tighter contract and your rationale is the right one: 0.95 (shared hard identifier) must stay distinguishable from 1.0 (certainty), and a recency boost on top of near-proof buys nothing while destroying that distinction. Boosting only the weak narrative/MO-only pairs is exactly where the temporal signal carries information. Do not change it. Please add a one-line comment in linkage.py citing this decision so the next reader doesn't "fix" it back.

2. FINGERPRINT jsonb — correct fix, and `_coerce_fingerprint()` on the read path is the right defensive move. Keep.

3. INGEST BRIDGE — keep it as the v2-owned endpoint. Do NOT touch v1. `POST /enterprise/ingest/case/{case_id}` with background execution is strictly better than an in-process call: it holds the zero-v1-change rule, keeps the latency-critical path clean, and makes the seam explicit and demoable. I'm making the demo runner the caller.

PATH CONVENTION — ruling, so Teams 2 and 5 don't diverge: `/enterprise/<resource>`, NO `/api/` segment, matching what you shipped. IMPLEMENTATION_PROMPT.md uses `/enterprise/api/...` in places; that's superseded. I've told frontend and I'm telling the new teams.

Pre-existing v1 lint violations: leave them. Correct call.

Two follow-ups for you while Teams 2 and 5 spin up:
a) Write `backend/migrations/README.md` (or extend it) with the exact steps to apply v2_enterprise.sql to Supabase, including the pgvector/`vector` extension prerequisite and how to verify the `graph_neighbours` RPC exists afterwards. The person applying it will not be you.
b) Confirm what happens on repeat application — you said idempotent; state explicitly whether re-running is safe with data already present.

Stay up; you're the integration reference for Teams 2 and 5 and I'll route their signature questions to you.
